institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have lived there before and really liked it, a lot of my friends live there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, although I knew a lot beforehand anyway as I lived in Vienna before.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were some general Intro days with general admin info for Austria and some for Boku, however it wasn't very thorough.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Quite easy, there are a lot of (free!) platforms you can check, for example
WGgesucht.at
(also an App) for flat shares, or home4students, ÖJAB and others for student dorms where you can apply. For normal flats there are also good websites like
Immosuche.at
,
willhaben.at
, or
Immosuchmaschine.at
. Compared to Kopenhagen its a lot easier to find a place to life, also on short term basis.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Well at BOKU there is no real Campus so you just search for something in the City, maybe check the public transport connections to BOKU as it is not very central (easily reachable but not central). Otherwise it is just a question of how far you want to commute and in what area you want to live, e.g. 18. and 19. District of Vienna are very nice but posh, the "cool" hip districts are 2,6,7,8, also very nice are 4,5,9,16,17,20.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to go to study services in Person once to get registered, it's mandatory to show up in Person. The rest is pretty simple, they send you the Documents you need to sign, and then you bring them and upload a foot for your ID card and then pay the student union fee (around 20€) directly at registration or online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online guidelines on the Boku website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check early on for appointments to register, then everything is smooth sailings.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot, and I mean a lot of courses at BOKU, but not all of them are good or actually match the course description

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were very basic and not different from Bachelor courses, others were much more specific than Bachelor courses but also not significantly harder to pass.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Worse, mostly frontal teaching so only lectures, often no connection to "Real life", not very hands on.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Aquatic biomonitoring and assessment
Ecological river landscape management
Human impacts on riverine landscapes
Ecology of aquatic systems
Integrated flood risk management
Mountain forest climatology and headwater hydrology
Multiple criterion decision making in natural resource management 
Plant and environment
Soil ecology
Risk assessment in the aquatic environment
Role of soils in nature conservation and wildlife management

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Research proposal
Master thesis seminar

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Aquatic biomonitoring and assessment, it's very nice and well structured, easy to pass but very interesting
Integrated flood risk management, also very interesting, very in depth
Human impacts in riverine LS and Ecological river LS management, they go together very well and provide a very good overview with a lot of specifics of the topic. 
Soil ecology, it is very well taught with different teaching methods

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's a football and basketball club, running circle, Yoga things and others at BOKU directly. However, Vienna wide there's USI sport courses offered by the University of Vienna available for all students which has a lot of very different courses (like football, climbing, sword fighting, capoeira, massage etc).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Look into USI courses, there's something there for everyone,

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other Austrian cities like Innsbruck, Salzburg, Linz and Graz, go to the countryside around Vienna, visit Bratislava, Budapest and Prague, as well as Hainburg and the Donauauen national park, go to Stammersdorf to some Winecellars, go to Neusiedlersee, go hiking in Rax, go swimming in the Danube, explore Donauinsel, bike along the Ring, go out at Gürtel, explore different coffeshops and bars...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it's my culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don´t be thrown off by harsh looking people at first. Also, being persistent helps to get closer to Austrians. Also, try to escape the Erasmus bubble and do other activities if you want to get to know more Austrian

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: angry viennese people, and accepting that's just how they are

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It's more laid back, and very nice for drinking etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not get frustrated with BOKU administration, you for sure will, find others to rant about it with and have a laugh
Explore Vienna, it has so much to offer, and also the surroundings (I can highly recommend going to some Heuriger) 
Be ready for a totally different system of university, you will have a lot of smaller courses, which also often overlap, don't panic about that

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don´t panic about overlapping courses when you first register, it's not a big problem.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends and getting to know the city and culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with the BOKU administration

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
